class_name: 自然発生-抑制不能-テシカタガナイ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Names a feeling that wells up on its own and will not be suppressed, and it takes spontaneous predicates readily (気になってならない, 思えてならない, 悔やまれてならない). Among its siblings it is the literary one and tends toward inner, often negative emotion, where てしかたがない is neutral and てたまらない bodily. It attaches to verb て, い-adjective くて, and noun or な-adjective で alike.

examples.ruby: 夜中[よなか]の物音[ものおと]が今[いま]も気[き]になってならない。
examples.english: That noise in the night still nags at me, and I can't shake it.

examples.ruby: この曲[きょく]を聴[き]くと、故郷[こきょう]の海[うみ]が懐[なつ]かしくてならない。
examples.english: Whenever I hear this song, I miss the sea back home more than I can bear.

examples.ruby: 祖父[そふ]に一言[ひとこと]も伝[つた]えられなかったのが残念[ざんねん]でならない。
examples.english: It grieves me no end that I never got to say a single word to my grandfather.

patterns.usage_note: Names a sensation or craving pushed past what can be endured: heat, itch, pain, hunger, or wanting something (暑くてたまらない, 会いたくてたまらない). It typically resists spontaneous predicates such as 思えて or 気になって, where てならない or てしかたがない are used instead. It is ordinary in casual speech and takes both welcome and unwelcome feelings; nouns and な-adjectives take で, い-adjectives くて.

examples.ruby: クーラーが壊[こわ]れて、部屋[へや]の中[なか]が暑[あつ]くてたまらない。
examples.english: The AC broke and the room is unbearably hot.

examples.ruby: 明日[あした]の面接[めんせつ]のことが不安[ふあん]でたまらない。
examples.english: I'm a nervous wreck about tomorrow's interview.

examples.ruby: 孫[まご]が初[はじ]めて名前[なまえ]を呼[よ]んでくれて、嬉[うれ]しくてたまらない。
examples.english: My grandchild said my name for the first time, and I couldn't be happier.

patterns.usage_note: Names a feeling or sensation too strong to control, and is the widest and most neutral member of this family, covering physical sensations, emotions, and spontaneous feelings alike (眠くてしかたがない, 心配でしかたがない). てたまらない is bodily, てならない literary and inward, てしょうがない casual. The full てしかたがない is slightly more formal than the clipped てしかたない.

examples.ruby: 隣[となり]の工事[こうじ]の音[おと]がうるさくてしかたない。
examples.english: The construction noise next door is driving me up the wall.

examples.ruby: 息子[むすこ]の帰[かえ]りが遅[おそ]く、心配[しんぱい]でしかたない。
examples.english: My son is late getting home, and I'm worried sick.

examples.ruby: 昼[ひる]を抜[ぬ]いたので、腹[はら]が減[へ]ってしかたない。
examples.english: I skipped lunch, so now I'm starving out of my mind.

patterns.usage_note: Names a feeling or state too strong to put up with, in casual speech; しょうがない is a worn-down しようがない (退屈でしょうがない). It usually reports an ongoing nuisance and carries a note of complaint, where てしかたがない is neutral and てならない literary. It is out of place in formal writing, which uses てしかたがない or てならない.

examples.ruby: 花粉[かふん]のせいで目[め]がかゆくてしょうがない。
examples.english: The pollen has my eyes itching like crazy.

examples.ruby: 同[おな]じ曲[きょく]が頭[あたま]の中[なか]でぐるぐる回[まわ]ってしょうがない。
examples.english: The same song keeps going round and round in my head and it's driving me nuts.

examples.ruby: 新[あたら]しい職場[しょくば]の人間[にんげん]関係[かんけい]が憂鬱[ゆううつ]でしょうがない。
examples.english: The politics at my new workplace get me down something awful.

patterns.usage_note: Names a situation that is a nuisance the speaker wishes were otherwise, close in force to て困る or てかなわない (肩が凝っていけない). It is old-fashioned; contemporary speakers usually say てしょうがない or てかなわない. The corpus rule licenses only verbs, but くていけない with い-adjectives (暑くていけない) is well attested. 〜てはいけない is a different pattern, prohibition rather than complaint.

examples.ruby: 窓[まど]の隙間[すきま]から風[かぜ]が入[はい]ってきていけない。
examples.english: A draft keeps coming in through the gap in the window, and it's a real nuisance.

examples.ruby: 歳[とし]を取[と]ると物忘[ものわす]れが増[ふ]えていけない。
examples.english: As you get on in years you forget more and more, and it's no good at all.

examples.ruby: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]は古傷[ふるきず]が痛[いた]んでいけない。
examples.english: On rainy days my old injury aches, and it's a bother.
